The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.

What We Value:

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

  • Seek Excellence.
  • Be Selective To Be Effective.
  • Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
  • Disagree Transparently.
  • Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
  • Build Dream Teams.

Who You Are

Compensation costs are a key driver of profitability for the data center business given revenues are contracted for 15-year periods and operating costs are passed through to tenants. This role will own the allocation, analysis and reporting of that information across data halls, between construction and operations, recoveries, etc. Within the Data Center team, you are a detail-oriented CPA with a genuine appetite for analysis. You will build and run the allocation models, reconcile them monthly, explain what is driving the numbers, and prepare the support that our accountants rely on to book entries. Over time you will take ownership of share-based compensation calculations and the related disclosures for our financial statements, proxy statements and other filings.

You will be trusted with highly confidential employee compensation information which you will handle with absolute discretion. You will regularly work directly with the Data Center Head of Finance and the Co-Heads of the Data Center business, presenting your analyses and fielding their questions. This role reports to the Head of FP&A – Data Centers, with a dotted-line relationship to the Controller. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with proven analytical skills and the judgment to know when a number needs a second look.

What You’ll Do:

Analysis & Insight

  • Build and maintain the models that allocate compensation and related costs at the individual employee level to the relevant data halls, projects, departments and legal entities
  • Analyze the capitalization versus expense split of compensation costs, and the resulting impact on operating cost pass-through, project cost and reported results
  • Prepare and regularly present monthly budget-to-actual, trend and headcount-driven variance analysis; explain the “why” behind the numbers to stakeholders and business leaders
  • Model headcount scenarios (hiring plans, transfers, ramp-up of new data halls) and their effect on cost, capitalization and tenant recovery to support budgeting and forecasting
  • Test the reasonableness of allocation drivers and methodologies, and recommend changes as the business evolves
  • Provide ad hoc analysis to support Data Center leadership, group finance, lender, tenant and reporting needs

Compensation Allocation & Capitalization

  • Identify compensation costs associated with construction and other qualifying activities that may be capitalized, and maintain the supporting methodology, driver- or time-based allocations and monthly attestations
  • Apply and help refine Galaxy’s compensation capitalization framework in accordance with US GAAP (e.g., ASC 360 and ASC 720-10-25-3), documenting conclusions for the Controller, Reporting team and external auditors
  • Track changes in headcount, role, location and responsibilities (new hires, transfers, terminations, promotions) and reflect them in allocations on a timely basis
  • Allocate ancillary and overhead costs such as occupancy, technology, T&E, benefits and payroll taxes, using defensible, consistently applied drivers

Share-Based Compensation & Disclosure

  • Assist with data center share-based compensation calculations (e.g., ASC 718 expense attribution, forfeitures, modifications and allocation to data center entities and activities)
  • Assist with the preparation of supporting schedules and disclosure drafts for financial statement footnotes, proxy statements and other required filings, working with SEC reporting, Legal and People teams

Close, Reconciliation & Journal Entry Support

  • Prepare clear, well-documented journal entry support and schedules for the accounting team to rely on in booking compensation, allocation and capitalization entries during the month-end and quarter-end close
  • Reconcile payroll, benefits and bonus accruals to the general ledger and to allocation models monthly, at the legal entity level, and investigate and resolve variances
  • Support the Controller’s team on accruals, intercompany and cross-entity charges, and construction-in-progress roll-forwards as they relate to capitalized compensation
  • Manage and respond to audit and SOX control requests related to compensation allocation, capitalization and share-based compensation

Process Improvement & Automation

  • Automate allocation, reconciliation and reporting workflows to the extent possible, replacing manual, spreadsheet-based processes with scalable, controlled solutions
  • Contribute to the configuration and data design of Workday and related systems so that allocation attributes (cost center, project, data hall) flow cleanly from HR through payroll to the general ledger
  • Document policies, procedures and controls over compensation allocation and capitalization

Partnership

  • Work hand in hand with the People team on headcount, compensation and organizational data, and on the timing and accuracy of payroll feeds
  • Partner closely with the Construction, DC Operations, Environmental Health & Safety, Technology, Power, and Growth & Development teams to understand how people spend their time and to validate allocations
  • Work closely with the Controller’s team, FP&A and SEC reporting on their requests and initiatives

What We’re Looking For:

  • CPA
  • Public accounting experience (audit or advisory), followed by 1+ years of experience in an industry accounting or financial analysis role
  • Proven analytical skills: ability to build models, find the story in large datasets and clearly explain findings to non-accountants
  • Advanced Excel experience (large datasets, lookups, pivots, reconciliations)
  • Strong working knowledge of US GAAP, particularly capitalization of internal costs (ASC 360 / ASC 720) and payroll-related accounting
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare clear, well-supported schedules and journal entry support that others can rely on
  • Unquestionable integrity and discretion in handling confidential employee compensation information
  • Strong attention to detail, with the discipline to reconcile and tie out data from multiple sources every month
  • Intellectually curious self-starter, comfortable navigating ambiguity and building process where none exists
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the poise and clarity to present analysis to senior leaders and the confidence to say when the data does not support a conclusion
  • Team-player attitude; able to build credibility across disparate teams
  • Ability to multitask and meet recurring close deadlines in a fast-paced, high-growth environment
  • Flexibility to innovate and implement new procedures to improve processes and workflow

Bonus Points: 

  • Experience with Workday (HCM or Financials)
  • Experience with payroll data and cost allocation models in real estate, construction, energy, telecom or data center environments
  • Experience with automation or analytics tools (VBA, Power Query, Power BI, Python or SQL)
  • Experience with cost recovery / CAM or pass-through billing under triple-net leases
  • Experience with share-based compensation accounting and related disclosure requirements

Who we are

About Stripe 

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team 

  • The Billing Foundations team builds the core infrastructure and data foundations that power Stripe Billing and support products across Stripe’s revenue and finance suite, including Tax. We build the shared systems that help these products scale, from real-time infrastructure for usage-based billing to customer balance management.
  • Our product is the infrastructure itself: the building blocks that product teams depend on to deliver reliable experiences for businesses. As usage-based business models evolve, including those powering AI products and agents, we’re solving technical challenges around scale, low latency, and strong system guarantees.
  • Product management on this team combines long-term technical strategy with a deep understanding of internal users’ needs. You’ll work closely with principal engineers and product teams across Stripe to shape shared infrastructure, make thoughtful platform tradeoffs, and build foundations that support the next generation of billing products.

What you’ll do 

You will work with engineering leadership to set a long-term vision for how our product infrastructure best supports the agent-led workflows of the next million Stripe Billing customers. Because our users are engineers and their agents, your deep technical product understanding is uniquely important to ensure successful onboarding, retention, and growth of our customer base.

Additionally, you are the steward for the technical and security aspects of our entire revenue and finance suite. You will ensure that our product is the fastest, most secure, and most reliable monetization infrastructure on the planet.

Responsibilities 

  • Set the strategy, vision, and outcomes for the Foundations team
  • Work directly with our most important clients to ensure that our product infrastructure and service-level agreements meet their needs
  • Partner deeply with engineering to make correct product and engineering tradeoffs as we build new products
  • Introduce new infrastructure products that advance our mission, such as Low Latency Streaming Billing and Margin-aware Event Pricing

Who you are 

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements 

  • 10+ years of product management experience, including experience owning and delivering complex products with substantial technical or domain depth
  • Experience operating as a senior individual contributor: independently setting direction, aligning cross-functional teams, and driving important decisions without relying on formal authority
  • Strong customer instincts and experience working directly with specialized users to uncover underlying needs and translate domain complexity into coherent products, supported by an understanding of complex systems, data models, application programming interfaces (APIs), integrations, and technical tradeoffs
  • Strong strategic judgment and experience taking products from ambiguity to execution: identifying differentiated advantages, defining initial markets, sequencing multi-year opportunities, and connecting strategy to detailed requirements, data analysis, and delivery
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and collaborative leadership across technical, business, and go-to-market teams, with the ability to clarify complex problems, align stakeholders, surface risks, and make or revise decisions as evidence changes in high-stakes environments

Preferred qualifications 

  • Familiarity with streaming systems
  • Experience managing infrastructure products with reliability of four nines or higher
  • An engineering background

About Alchemy

Alchemy is the Web3 infrastructure and developer platform that powers millions of users and the world’s most innovative blockchain applications. From enabling $1+ trillion in financial transactions worldwide to scaling L2s and enabling DeFi, Alchemy provides the infrastructure and tools developers need to build reliable, scalable, and accessible experiences.

Trusted by companies like JPMorgan, Stripe, Visa, Franklin Templeton, Nike, and backed by a16z, Coatue, Silver Lake, Lightspeed, and Stanford University, Alchemy is building the foundational layer for a decentralized and AI-enabled Web3 ecosystem. For more information, visit alchemy.com.

 

The Role

We're looking for a Security Operations Engineer to improve how Alchemy detects threats, investigates incidents, and reduces operational security risk. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role with no people-management responsibilities.

You'll investigate suspicious activity and build the systems that make the next investigation faster and more reliable. AI-assisted engineering and investigation should be part of your daily work: connecting evidence, developing detections, building response workflows, and checking the results against source data.

You'll also help the team get better at this work. Through shared tooling, code review, pairing, and practical documentation, you'll give teammates capabilities they can use independently.

 

What You Will Do

  • Detect and investigate threats. Triage alerts, hunt for suspicious activity, and investigate across cloud infrastructure, corporate systems, identity, endpoints, and production environments. Establish what happened from evidence and communicate uncertainty clearly.

  • Engineer detection coverage. Build and tune detections, onboard useful telemetry, and maintain reliable log pipelines. Test rules against representative attacks and benign activity; address missing coverage and noisy alerts.

  • Respond to incidents. Participate in the security on-call rotation and incident response, including scoping, containment, recovery, and post-incident improvements. Preserve evidence and coordinate changes with system owners.

  • Build AI-assisted security workflows. Automate evidence collection, alert enrichment, investigation timelines, and response preparation. Connect agents to approved tools and data sources so they can complete bounded tasks with traceable results.

  • Verify before trusting. Evaluate AI-assisted workflows against known cases and adversarial inputs. Require evidence for conclusions, test false-positive and missed-threat behavior, and keep human approval for disruptive containment actions.

  • Reduce operational exposure. Partner with Infrastructure and IT on vulnerability remediation, cloud and host hardening, identity controls, and attack-surface monitoring. Prioritize findings by exposure and impact, then verify remediation.

  • Help secure agent operations. Work with platform and product-security partners on operational controls for agent identities, credentials, tool access, and audit logging. Investigate misuse and build detections for suspicious agent behavior.

  • Improve how the team works. Share reusable code, investigation skills, runbooks, and evaluation cases. Pair with teammates, review automation, and teach approaches they can apply to their own investigations.

  • Measure defensive outcomes. Track detection coverage, alert quality, investigation effort, response time, and remediation progress. Use those measures to decide what to improve next.

     

What We Are Looking For

  • Hands-on security operations experience spanning detection engineering, threat hunting, and incident response.

  • Strong scripting and software-building ability, especially Python; experience with APIs, version control, tests, and operating automation in production.

  • Experience with a SIEM such as Panther, Splunk, or an equivalent platform, including detection logic and log analysis.

  • Working knowledge of cloud security, identity, endpoint telemetry, networking, and Linux systems. Ability to investigate across system boundaries.

  • Evidence of building and using AI-assisted tools in security or adjacent engineering work. You can show how you validate outputs, handle failures, and protect sensitive information.

  • Sound incident judgment: you can separate a hypothesis from a finding, preserve evidence, and choose when to escalate or contain.

  • A record of making teammates more effective through tools, mentoring, code review, or documentation, without needing management authority.

  • Clear written communication and the willingness to own both urgent investigations and the follow-through that prevents repeat incidents.

 

Helpful Experience

  • AWS, Kubernetes, bare-metal infrastructure, detection-as-code, or SOAR workflows.

  • Digital forensics, threat intelligence, or testing detections through attack simulation.

  • Securing AI agents and tool integrations, including prompt injection, credential misuse, and data-exfiltration risks.

  • Blockchain infrastructure or other environments with sensitive keys and high-impact production systems.

     

What Success Looks Like

  • Investigations reach evidence-backed conclusions faster. Detection coverage improves, repeat noise declines, and remediation is verified. The team adopts tools and workflows you've built, with clear limits on what agents may do and a tested path for handling failures.

At Ripple, we’re building a world where value moves like information does today. It’s big, it’s bold, and we’re already doing it. THE WORK:

Capital markets still settle on infrastructure built decades ago. Trillions of dollars in fund assets sit idle in settlement delays and collateral buffers because no rail can move legal title in real time. We are building that rail on the XRP Ledger, and it is already live: tokenized funds exist on XRPL today as Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTs), moving as collateral across issuance, distribution and repo with some of the world's largest asset managers and custodians.

You will own the two protocol workstreams that decide how far this goes.

Token standards. MPTs need to grow from a fund token into a complete issuance framework for institutions: asset restrictions, corporate events, programmable behavior. Get this right and the next wave of assets (commercial paper, commodities, bonds, equities) can be issued, held and mobilized natively on a public ledger. Each asset class brings its own rules, and you will determine what fits within the protocol and what remains outside it.

Privacy. Institutions will not trade on a ledger where every position is visible. Confidential MPT brings capital-markets-grade confidentiality to a public chain. You will be responsible for its progress from initial rollout to enterprise-wide adoption. This covers keeping up with new emerging technologies and industry trends, and working with custodians and wallets supporting development into vaults and payments. These are open problems across the industry. Few teams anywhere in the world are working on all of them at once.

This is a role where you witness your impact directly. The specifications you write become amendments to an open-source ledger, adopted by the XRPL validators community and used by real institutions moving real money. You will work alongside protocol engineers, cryptographers, custodians and issuers, with the backing of a team that has already brought the first institutional funds on-chain.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Lead the tokenization roadmap for XRPL: MPT evolution, transfer controls, corporate actions and programmable tokens, and decide what belongs in the protocol versus above it.
  • Lead the privacy roadmap: take Confidential MPTs from mainnet launch to institutional scale, including key rotation and recovery, performance targets and confidential vaults.
  • Generate new feature specifications and build the consensus behind them, working with Ripple engineering, XRPL validators and open-source contributors to carry proposals from concept to amendment.
  • Set the requirements and priorities for each new asset class, and shape the go-to-market that brings capital markets participants onto XRPL.
  • Make new primitives usable, not just live: bring hardware wallets, custodians and issuer platforms along so institutions can adopt on day one.
  • Scope the compliance capabilities that regulated issuers need to meet their obligations on XRPL.
  • Partner with developer growth and documentation teams so institutions can originate assets on XRPL without a Ripple engineer in the room.
  • Define the metrics that show the work is landing: XRPL's share of tokenized assets, issuance volume and ecosystem integrations.

In your first 90 days, you will take charge of a single roadmap across tokenization and privacy and know every open item on it. By the end of your first year, you will have successfully delivered the next generation of tokenization capabilities. And outlined what institutional privacy on XRPL entails.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING: 

  • Experience shipping technical platform or protocol products as a product manager, typically six or more years, with a record of taking complex things from idea to adoption.
  • Comfort with protocol-level design: you can work through ledger internals, token standards and cryptography-adjacent questions (confidential transactions, key management) alongside engineers, and you enjoy learning the parts you do not know yet.
  • Clear writing: specifications, requirements and positioning that bring engineers, partners and executives to the same page.
  • A collaborative way of working: you build alignment across distributed teams and partners, and you are comfortable shaping the roadmap when the answers are not yet known.

This role owns the legal work that moves a site from a land position to an energized facility: acquisitions, leases and easements; water rights and supply; utility, interconnection and energy management arrangements; long-lead electrical equipment; and the entitlements and regulatory approvals each site depends on.

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

TRM helps financial institutions detect and stop illicit finance, and this role brings that mission to private sector clients including banks, payment providers, crypto natives and fintechs across Central & Eastern Europe and Central Asia. You will own the Private Sector business in a territory where TRM is building coverage, setting account strategy and strategic deals with compliance and risk leaders. What makes this seat unusual is a large greenfield territory plus the freedom to shape your own go-to-market with local partners and AI-assisted research.

The impact you will have:

  • Open new private sector accounts across CEE and Central Asia. Working with internal and external stakeholders to build effective networks to deliver commercial execution of TRM’s services to leading private sector organisations across the region.

  • Win a mixture of high velocity and larger more strategic engagements, by turning AML and fraud pain points into a clear business case, with AI-drafted account plans and proposals that you sharpen with your own market judgment.

  • Own and define the model to build a 3x qualified pipeline each quarter through targeted campaigns, using AI-assisted segmentation and local-language messaging, and measure what converts.

  • Decide how TRM enters each market, choosing between direct selling, resellers, and regional partners, and back each choice with AI-assisted analysis of account data.

  • Grow strategic existing customers engagements through renewals, upsells, and new use cases.

  • Bring customer and regulatory insight back to Product and Marketing so the next release matches how banks in your region actually work.

What we’re looking for:

  • 5+ years selling SaaS or data products into banks, payment firms, crypto or fintechs in CEE or Central Asia, or 4+ years with deep AML and financial crime expertise, plus experience using AI tools to research and prioritize accounts.

  • A record of closing a mixture of quick deal cycle and strategic longer term, higher value engagements and meeting quota, with AI-supported forecasting and pipeline reviews.

  • Working knowledge of regional AML and sanctions frameworks and how compliance, risk, and procurement teams buy.

  • Hands-on use of AI for prospecting, account planning, and call preparation, with clear examples of time or revenue gained.

  • Experience building pipeline in a new territory, forming human lead networks and AI-assisted tools to test and measure what works.

  • Credible, clear communication with senior compliance and risk executives, in person and virtually, including AI-assisted preparation for each meeting.

  • Fluent English; Russian or a CEE relevant language is a strong plus.

  • Based in Poland and willingness to travel regularly across the region.

About the Team:

  • TRM’s EMEA Sales team gives each Account Director full ownership of a territory and the room to choose how to win it.

  • The team collaborates closely and supports one another through shared pipeline insight, deal reviews, and open sharing of what works.

  • The work is hard in a useful way: regulated buyers, several countries, long procurement cycles, and a product category that is still new to many banks.

  • You will work with RevOps, Marketing, Legal, Product, and Solutions Architecture, who move quickly to back your deals.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within your first 30 days, you rank every target bank and fintech in your territory and start outreach to the top tier, so pipeline grows before onboarding ends.

  • When a compliance leader asks for a demo late on a Friday, you and TRM’s Solutions team deliver it that day, turning a warm inquiry into a scheduled evaluation by Monday.

  • Within 90 days, you build qualified pipeline worth at least 3x your quota, backed by an account plan for every Tier 1 target.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Distributed, not distant: the team works across UK and CET time zones, with flexibility for Central Asia hours and occasional US calls on complex deals.

  • Slack is the center of day-to-day communication. @mention colleagues for timely responses.

  • Weekly 1:1 with your manager, a weekly team call, a weekly pipeline call, a weekly forecast call, and regular pod calls.

  • Company-wide all-hands and founder Q&A sessions keep everyone connected to the mission.

Required online and collaboration hours:

  • Schedule: Core hours overlapping CET, with flexibility for Central Asia hours and occasional US calls.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. Great stories start with extraordinary people.

We’re bringing together exceptional creative talent to tell the stories of people shaping the future. Work alongside people who raise your standards, champion your ideas, and give you room to do the best work of your career.

Story inspires science. Science makes story real.

Your Story

We're looking for a Producer who knows how to make the impossible happen.

Someone who's relentless, resourceful, and doesn't take no for an answer. You know how to stretch a small budget into something extraordinary, navigate complex productions, and find creative solutions when the obvious ones don't work.

At Story, you'll lead Masters of Movies, a new cinematic interview series in which Jason Carman sits down for two-to-three-hour conversations with the people who make great movies: directors, composers, actors, VFX artists, etc. Between them sits a monitor with the guest's films loaded in, so they can pull up scenes and walk through the craft together. We want to keep the craft of cinema alive, and respect it. A serious, unhurried conversation with the people who make the great films.

One week, you might be working the phones with agents and publicists to land a legendary director in the middle of a release cycle. The next week, you're building a set in New York or LA (C-stands, cinema cameras, a dark background) and making sure every scene cues up flawlessly on camera. You thrive at both ends of it.

What You'll Own

  • Make it happen. Take productions from concept to delivery. Find solutions, open doors, and keep pushing when things get difficult.

  • Run multiple productions. Manage several projects simultaneously, balancing budgets, schedules, crews, and competing priorities without losing track of the details.

  • Build exceptional crews. Find, hire, and manage talented freelancers, production partners, and vendors across different markets.

  • Make every dollar count. Own budgets, negotiate rates, and find creative ways to deliver ambitious work with limited resources.

  • Solve the hard problems. Secure difficult locations, navigate tight timelines, handle last-minute changes, and find a way forward when the original plan falls apart.

  • Lead on set. Run efficient, professional shoots, keeping crews aligned, guests comfortable, and the creative vision intact. Work with Wizard to make sure the on-set product experience works flawlessly.

  • Be a creative partner. Work closely with directors and cinematographers to figure out what's possible and find better ways to execute it.

  • Book the guests. Coordinate guests and negotiate their appearances. Many will come through film-release promotion cycles, so timing and relationships matter.

  • Get every episode out the door. Work with the editorial team from shoot through delivery.

  • Grow the audience. Own marketing and distribution: the launch plan, shorts and clips from each episode, guest cross-promotion, and audience growth.

  • Prep the host. Give Jason the guest research and the films to load into Wizard before each interview.

  • Be our voice in Hollywood. As the show grows, become the official liaison between Wizard and the Hollywood and entertainment community.

Your First Six Months

  • Three excellent episodes in the can.

  • A repeatable production playbook: booking, travel, set build, shoot, edit, release.

  • A guest pipeline beyond the first three.

You're the Right Person If

  • You have significant experience producing or showrunning talent-driven shows, documentaries, commercials, or other high-end video productions, ideally with minimal staff.

  • You've worked on both large-budget productions and lean, independent shoots. You're equally comfortable in both.

  • You're exceptionally resourceful. When someone says a location, shot, or idea isn't possible, your instinct is to find another way.

  • You're proactive and decisive. You don't wait for someone to tell you what needs to happen next.

  • You can juggle multiple productions at different stages without letting anything slip through the cracks.

  • You're a strong negotiator who knows how to get the most out of a budget without compromising relationships or quality.

  • You have a real phone book in film. You know, or can quickly reach, the agents, publicists, and people around major directors, composers, and actors, along with a trusted network of crew and vendors.

  • You stay calm under pressure and take ownership when things go wrong.

  • You're comfortable owning marketing and building an audience for a show.

What Sets You Apart

You have a relentless production instinct. You don't stop at the first no. You make another call, find another contact, negotiate a better deal, or come up with an entirely different approach.

You're scrappy without sacrificing quality. You can produce a beautiful film with a five-person crew and a shoestring budget, then turn around and manage a large-scale production with the same confidence.

You care about the work. You're not just checking boxes and managing logistics. You have taste, creative instincts, and genuine pride in what ends up on screen. You know what makes a great interview and a great film conversation.

You take ownership. You anticipate problems before they happen. You don't need to be chased for updates, and you don't pass problems off to someone else. You see things through.

You make everyone around you better. Guests trust you, crews want to work with you, and Jason walks into every interview prepared because you're running the show.

Compensation
